IS* 3743 -1966 

Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
HAIR CLIPPERS ( HAND-OPERATED ) 

0. FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution 
on 26 September 1966, after the draft finalized by the Cutlery Sectional 
Committee had been approved by the Consumer Products Division 
Council. 

0.2 This standard dealing with the hair clippers ( hand-operated ) is one of 
a scries of Indian Standard specifications on cutlery items formulated at the 
instance of the Chief Inspectorate of General Stores ( Miristry of Defence ) 
and Office of the Development Commissioner, Small Scale Industries. 
Other standards published so far in the series are given at page 12. 

0.3 Hair clippers have been in use for a few decades in the country, but 
their manufacture has been taken up recently. In order to help regulating 
the production to standardized materials, design and performance, this 
standard has been prepared. Under this class of appliarces come animal 
hair clippers both hand-operated and propulsion-operated. Specifications 
for these appliances are also being drawn up. 

0.4 In the preparation of this standard, assistance has been derived from the 
following: 

CSDS/T&I/ 14(b) Clippers, hair, No. «0\ Chief Inspectorate of 
General Stores, Ministry of Defence, Government of Irdia. 

GGG-C-475 : 1954 Clippers, hair, hand. Federal Supply ^Service. 
W6A. 

0.5 This standard contains clauses which call for agreement between the 
purchaser and the supplier and which permit the purchaser to use his 
option for selection to suit his requirements. The relevant clauses 
are 4.1 and 11.1. 

0.6 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this 
standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing 
the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS: 2-1960* 
The number 6f significant places retained in the rounded off value should 
be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 

+Rutes for rounding off numerical values ( retnud).

1. 8COPE 

1*1 This standard covers manually-operated hair clippers ordinarily used 
by hair dressers for dressing human hair.

4. DESIGN AND DIMENSIONS 

4.1 The hair clippers shall generally conform to the design as given in 
Fig. 1 and 2. The detailed designs and shapes of component parts are left 
to the discretion of manufacturers and are subject to the agreement between 
the purchaser and the supplier. 

4*2 The teeth in the top and bottom plates shall be made as shown in 
Fig. 3 and 4. The pitch of the teeth shall be as given below: 

Commercial Size Designation Pitch of Tetth 

mm 

No. 1 2'0 

No. 1-5 

No. 00 1-5 

No. 000 1-5 

No. 0000 1-2 

5. CONSTRUCTION 

5.1 The hair clippers shall be convenient to operate and made to com- 
mercial sfees^as given in 2.1. 

5.2 The hair clippers shall consist of a top plate and a bottom plate with 
comb-like teeth (cutting plate), a fixed arm, a movable arm, two small 
screws, one clamping screw, a wing nut and a spring, a spring washer, a cover 
plate, a screw cup, a screw driver and a mandrel (see Fig. 1, 2 and 5 ). 

53 Arms shall be of a suitable shape for effective grip with thumb rest on 
left handle and finger rest on right handle. Arrangement, such as a provi- 
sion of a wing nut shall be made for varying pressure or tension on the 
top and bottom plates without the use of tools. 

5.4 An easily detachable cover for cutting edges shall be provided to each 
hair clippers.

6. MANUFACTURE 

6.1 Both ilic arms and the cap of the hair clippers shall be soundly die cast 
The cap shall he properly made so that it is possible to fix it on the top 
plate and to withdraw it easily. The cap may be fitted with ball* or pro* 
vided with lugs to serve as bearing on the top surface of the top plate. The 
teeth shall be cut true, accurate and even in spacing. The spring, spring 
washer and the cutting plates shall be properly and evenly beat-treated. 



8

74 The top and bottom plates, spring and spring washer shall be uniformly 
and evenly hardened and tempered to hardness as shown against each: 

Top and bottom f 700 to 800 HV for size No. 1 

plates ( 650 to 700 HV for size 0, 00, 000 and 0000 
Spring 400 to 500 HV 

Spring washer 450 to 550 HV 

8. WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 

8*1 The die cast arm shall be free from pits, blow holes and like defects. 
The surfaces shall be dressed smooth. All other components shall be free 
from cracks, seams, flaws and all edges shall be smooth except the cutting 
edges. 

8.2 The teeth'shall be clean and bright, free from nicks, burrs and feathers, 
properly sharpened and ready for immediate use. The working ends 
bearing against each other shall be flat, smoothly ground and finely 
finished. 

8«3 There shall be no undue stiffness, shake, play or chatter between the 
moving parts. The clippers shall operate conveniently and smoothly. 

8.4 Finish — All exposed surfaces except the cutting edges and mild steel 
parts shall be plated chromium over nickel. The plating shall be even and 
uniform throughout and shall be polished bright. The plated surfaces shall 
be free from visible plating defects, such as blisters, pits, unplafed spots, 
cracks or stains. The plating shall be firm non.porous and shall not 
peel off. 

8.4.1 The plating shall conform to Grade B of IS : 1068-1958*. 

9. MARKUP 

9.1 The hair clippers shall be legibly and indelibly marked with the manu- 
facturer's name, initials or registered trademark and the words c Made in 
India 9 . 

9.1.1 The hair clippers may also be marked with the ISI Certification 
Mark. 

Nora — The use of the ISI Certification Mark is governed by the provident of the 
Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Maria ) Act, and the Rule* and Refutations 
made thereunder. Presence of this mark on products covered by an Indian Standard 
conveys the atfttrance thai they have been produced to comply with the rtquiromntt of 



-*- 



•Spedfication lor copper, nickel and chromium electroplated eoatiap.

UtS743-lN6 

that standard* under a well-defined ■yitcm of inspection, testing and quality control 
during production. This system, which is devised and supervised by ISI and operated 
by the producer, has the further safeguard that the products as actually marjeeted are 
continuously checked by ISI for conformity to the standard. Details of con di tion s, 
under which a licence for the use of the ISI Certification Mark may be granted to nunufac- 
turers or processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution. 

10. PACKING 

10.1 The cutting edges of hair clippers shall be treated with a suitable rust 
preventive and the hair clippers wrapped in tissue paper or placed in 
polyethylene bag and packed separately in a carton designating the sige of 
the clippers, manufacturer's name or trade-mark and the country of 
manufacture. 

11. SAMPLING 

11.1 Sampling and acceptance criteria for hair clippers shall be as agreed 
to between the purchaser ar*d the supplier. A recommended scheme for 
the same is given in Appendix A. 

12. TEST 

12*1 The hair clippers shall be subjected to practical user's test. The clip* 
pers shall cut the hair evenly without drag or pull leaving hair on the skin 
as given in 2.1. 

APPENDIX A 

(Clause 11.1) 

RECOMMENDED SAMPLING SCHEME AND CRITERIA FOR 
CONFORMITY FOR HAIR CUPPERS 

A-l. LOT 

A-l.I In any consignment, all the hair clippers of the same size, designation 
and manufactured from the same raw materials under relatively similar 
conditions of manufacture shall be grouped together to constitute a lot. 

A-l .2 For ascertaining the conformity to the requirements of this standard, 
sample of clippers shall be selected and tested separately for each lot. 

A-2. SELECTION OF SAMPLE 

A-2.1 The number of hair clippers to be selected at random from a lot shall 
depend upon the size of the lot and shall be in accordance with col 1 and 2 
of Table I.

A-2.2 The hair clippers in the sample shall be selected at random from the 
lot and in order to ensure the randomness of selection random number 
tables shall be used. In case random number tables are not available, the 
following procedure may by adopted: 

Starting from any clipper in the lot count them as 1, 2, 3 up 

to r and so on in one order, where r is the integral part of Ji/n (N 
being the lot size and n being the number of clippers to be selected ). 
Every rth clipper thus counted shall be withdrawn to give sample for 
test. 

JU3. NUMBER OF TESTS AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY 

A-3.1 All the clippers selected according to A-2.1 and A-2.2 shall be ins* 
pected for materials ( see 3.1 ), design and dimensions ( see 4.1 and 4.2), 
construction (see 5), manufacture ( see 6.1 ), hardness ( see 7.1 ), workman- 
ship and firiisn ( see 8 ), and tested for practical user's test ( see 12.1 ). 

A-3.2 The lot shall be declared conforming to the requirements of this 
standard, if the number of clippers found defective for one or more of the 
requirements mentioned in A-3.1 is less than or equal to the corresponding 
acceptance number given in col 3 of Table 1.
